inline.s: [The knowing of emptiness and stillness] is also called the numinous knowing. [To realize that all marks are empty, the mind is naturally without thought; when a thought arises, immediately be aware of it, and being aware, it is gone. The wondrous gate of practice lies entirely in this.] To realize that all marks are illusory, the mind is naturally without thought (this is the dream-illusion contemplation spoken of earlier). If a deluded thought arises, you must at once realize that it is taking illusion as real and being turned by illusory marks. Realizing this, the deluded thought instantly vanishes (this requires the power of concentration to cut off delusion on the spot; the practice is precisely in this). The wondrous gate of practice is right here!
Realizing that all marks are empty, the mind is naturally without thought; when a thought arises, be aware of it, and being aware, it goes away.”
This is the very essence of concentration and wisdom in union!

blocks.text: 3. Not letting go of a single thought, passing through every thought

inline.s: In investigating [the huatou], what is prized is true practice and actual realization, in order to put an end to birth and death. Not letting go of a single thought — that is true practice; passing through every thought — that is actual realization. In daily activity, not apart from a single dharma, not settled in a single dharma, at every point not letting go, passing through each one — this is genuine effort.

[Not letting go] That is, not being deluded by it. [Passing through] That is, not being enveloped by it, not going along with its manipulations, not taking it as a real thing, and still less being held hostage by it.
Master Hanshan instructed:
Practitioners of recent times are ever farther from the sages and do not see the true practice-walk of the ancients,
(that is)

but in the realms manifest in daily use, at the brink of birth and death, pass through each and every one. This very daily use — not apart from a single dharma, not settled in a single dharma, at every point not lightly letting go — is genuine effort. Wherever in the present sounds and forms, favorable and adverse, loved and hated realms, you are able to pass through each one, that is the true gateway of awakening. And in this very awakening, head after head and dharma after dharma, is the real Buddha-dharma.

If you can, at the points in daily use where thoughts arise and stir, where the root of feeling is firmly knotted, where love and hate interlace and are hard to untie, where the habitual tendencies of greed, anger, delusion, and pride are hard to wear away — there, at the very root of the pain, plant an awl
(same as ‘pierce’)
and investigate each and every one to the bottom,
(as dream, illusion, bubble, shadow)
passing through each one,
(cutting off deluded thoughts)
this is true knowledge
(this is to be a true good and wise friend)
; and then at once you ascend to the unhindered, freely at ease, great liberation, the supreme dharma-gate. Apart from this, what other knowledge
(good and wise friend)
is there to consult
(to seek out)
? What more extraordinary dharma-gate is there to enter?”
(See the notes in
True Practice, Real Realization
the essay

In the study of concentration and wisdom in union, there is a very important lesson: seeing is just seeing, hearing is just hearing, being aware is just being aware, knowing is just knowing, without giving rise to thoughts. — Not grasping at marks, still and unmoved in Thusness.
According to the Theravada scripture, the Udana:

There was a practitioner named Bahiya, who after a long, dusty journey arrived at Savatthi to seek the Dharma from the Buddha. Just then he saw the Buddha going door to door in the city for alms, every movement graceful and sublime, with the six sense faculties fully tamed, guarded, and at peace. Bahiya drew near, bowed at his feet, and asked the Buddha to teach him the Dharma — to teach him the Dharma of immeasurable benefit and peace. The Buddha said that he was then going door to door for alms and it was not fitting to teach. But Bahiya pleaded repeatedly, and so the Buddha taught him on the spot:

“Bahiya! You should train thus: in seeing, only what is seen; in hearing, only what is heard; in knowing, only what is known; in being aware, only what is aware. Bahiya! When you can be such that in seeing only the seen, in hearing only the heard, in knowing only the known, in being aware only the aware, then you will have reached freedom from attachment and obstruction. If you are free from attachment and obstruction, then you have no past life and no future life. You have not these two lives of past and future
(but only the present)
; all sorrow, lamentation, distress, and suffering will thereby be dispersed and vanish.”

[The three times] The past, present, and future. Whatever has arisen and ceased is called the ‘past’; whatever has arisen and not yet ceased is called the ‘present’; whatever has not been born and not yet arisen is called the ‘future’. [But only the present] The scripture says:
“In seeing, only the seen; in hearing, only the heard; in knowing, only the known; in being aware, only the aware.”
and without deluded thoughts about past or future. Indeed, the unease, anxiety, and suffering in people’s minds all arise from deluded imaginings about the past or the future.

blocks.text: 4. Dissolving karma, eradicating offenses, and bestowing blessings

inline.s: The Sutra of the Contemplation of the Practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva says:
“The ocean of all karmic hindrances is born of deluded thought. If you wish to repent, sit upright and contemplate reality. All offenses are like frost and dew — the sun of wisdom can dispel them.”
ocean of karmic hindrances
Karmic hindrances as deep and vast as the great sea.
all offenses like frost and dew, the sun of wisdom can dispel them
Just as the sun melts away frost and dew, contemplating reality (the sun of wisdom) can dispel all offenses.
As for “
contemplating reality
”, Master Hanshan explained
“A mind with no things is called reality.”
see
Essentials of Chan and Pure Land
, the chapter ‘The Sun of Wisdom Dispels Offenses’)

The mind that is without thought is a mind without things; sitting upright without thought is like the sun melting snow, frost, and dew — dissolving karma and eradicating offenses. This is repentance through reality:

“Offenses arise from the mind, so repent with the mind; when the mind is gone, offenses too are extinguished. When both the mind and its offenses are gone, both are empty — this is called true repentance.”
In the chapter ‘The Sun of Wisdom Dispels Offenses’, Master Hanshan instructed:

[Now, being in the dream of ignorance, how can one dissolve past karma? One must use the light of wisdom to break through ignorance, and be certain that one’s own mind is originally pure, not driven by deluded, inverted thought; then all karma has no cause, for deluded thought is the cause of all karma. Why is this? Because from beginningless time one has been deluded about one’s own mind, and life after life, with a deluded mind, created all sorts of karma. These karmic habits accumulate within the field of the eight consciousnesses, watered by the water of ignorance, so that this evil seed sprouts karmic shoots. This is the root of offense, and all evil karma arises from it.]

So now, being in the dream of ignorance, how can one dissolve past karma? One must use the light of wisdom to break through ignorance, be certain that one’s own mind is originally pure, and not be driven by deluded, inverted thought. Then there is no cause for creating karma, for deluded thought is the cause of all karma. Why is this? Because from beginningless kalpas one has been deluded about one’s own mind, and life after life, with a deluded mind, created all sorts of karma. These karmic habits accumulate in the alaya-vijnana (the eighth consciousness), watered by the water of ignorance, so that this evil seed sprouts karmic shoots. This is the root of offense, and all evil karma arises from it.
[Now, to dissolve past karma, you must first rouse the great light of wisdom to break through ignorance, not allowing deluded thoughts to sprout and grow in secret.
If you can, at the very point where a deluded thought arises, cut it off with a single thought, then the accumulated root of past karma is dissolved on the spot.

As the saying goes, do not fear the arising of thoughts, only fear that awareness is too slow. If awareness comes a little too late, then one is turned by them. If you can, at the points in daily use where thoughts arise and stir, be aware thought after thought and extinguish thought after thought, this is what is meant by ‘all offenses are like frost and dew — the sun of wisdom can dispel them’. Since the darkness of ignorance can be broken only by wisdom, this is what is meant by wisdom being able to dispel them.]
Now, to dissolve past karma, you must first rouse the great light of wisdom to break through ignorance, not allowing deluded thoughts to sprout and grow in secret.
If you can, at the very point where a deluded thought arises, cut it off with a single thought, then the root of karma accumulated in the past is dissolved on the spot.

As the saying goes, ‘do not fear the arising of thoughts, only fear that awareness is too slow’. If awareness comes a little too late, then one is turned by it (deluded thought). If you can, at the points in everyday life where thoughts arise and stir, be aware thought after thought and extinguish thought after thought, this is ‘all offenses are like frost and dew — the sun of wisdom can dispel them’. Since the darkness of ignorance can be broken only by wisdom, this is how wisdom is able to dispel all offenses.

[If, day and night without ceasing, you diligently observe and do not let it pass, then right at the place where deluded thought arises, you investigate to the very bottom the mark of non-arising. Looking again and again, in the end it is unobtainable. After a long time it becomes familiar and mature, and your own mind is pure and without things; a mind without things is reality. If you constantly contemplate this mind, what deluded thought could be accommodated, what accumulated karma could find lodging? This way of using the mind is called the samadhi of contemplation-and-observation.]

You must, day and night without ceasing, diligently observe and not let it pass, but right at the place where deluded thought arises, investigate to the very bottom the mark of non-arising. Looking again and again, the deluded thought is in the end unobtainable. After a long time it becomes familiar and mature, and your own mind is pure and without things,
a mind without things is reality

. If you constantly contemplate this pure mind, what deluded thought could be accommodated, what accumulated karma could find lodging? This way of using the mind is called the samadhi of contemplation-and-observation.

[If, day and night without ceasing, diligently observe] Here ‘ruo’ means ‘you’. For example: ‘If we change your service and restore your levy, then what do you say?’ (This line is from Liu Zongyuan’s ‘The Snake-Catcher’; rendered as: ‘Change your task of catching snakes and restore your tax levy — how would you find that?’)
Master Hanshan further instructed:
“Therefore the Buddha-dharma teaches people, first of all, to
(exclusively to)
make the severing of deluded thought the foundation,
(because)

deluded thought is the root of all manner of evil karma such as greed, anger, and delusion. Even the bodhisattva’s practice leading to Buddhahood, reaping the most sublime, adorned, and vast field of blessings in heaven and among humans, all begins with severing deluded thought.
As
(because)
deluded thought being severed, evil karma is dissolved; evil karma being dissolved, a hundred blessings gather. This is what is meant by seeking abundant blessings for oneself.
(from the Collected Works of a Dream-Wanderer
for Zhong Hengying)
